intent: Split the 356-line _transcribe_diarize.py into media probing, clustering maths, and the diarization pipeline, all under the 250-line cap, moving every definition verbatim.
scope: New: _transcribe_media.py 143 (duration probing, ffmpeg transcode, temp cleanup)
changes: Extracted _try_import, both duration probes, get_media_duration, the ffmpeg transcode and _cleanup_temp into _transcribe_media.py; _resample_linear, _kmeans_cosine and _run_kmeans_iterations into _transcribe_cluster.py. What remains in _transcribe_diarize.py is the pipeline: loading audio, loading the classifier, extracting embeddings, and diarize_segments.
The dependency graph is a tree: _transcribe_media imports nothing local, _transcribe_cluster imports only _try_import from it, and _transcribe_diarize imports from both.

transcribe_fw.py now imports get_media_duration from _transcribe_media rather than through _transcribe_diarize. This was forced by ruff removing the now-unused re-export, and is the correct outcome under the no-barrels rule - import sites should name the owning module.

Test modules were re-pointed to the module that owns each function. The audio tests span two modules: _load_audio stayed put and still patches its own namespace, while the direct transcode and cleanup calls now name _transcribe_media.

verification.evidence: IDENTICAL: all 13 top-level definitions moved verbatim. Re-run after ruff's autofixes and the import re-point, and still identical.

verification.command: AST scan for names used but not bound in each of the three modules
verification.evidence: All three report no unbound names, confirming the three module-level constants (_NDIM_2D, _SAMPLE_RATE_16K, _MIN_SAMPLES_DIAR) travelled to the modules that use them.
63 passed - the same count as before the split. _transcribe_cluster.py 51 statements / 18 branches, _transcribe_diarize.py 81 / 22, _transcribe_media.py 59 / 12, all 100%.

Exit 2, the code transcribe.sh branches on, and --help exits 0. This is what caught a real breakage: ruff had removed the get_media_duration re-export as unused, and transcribe_fw.py imported it from there. Only running it (and the full suite) surfaced that.
338 passed, unchanged from before the split.
All hooks pass. The shebang-executable hook reads the git index rather than the filesystem, so the new modules' mode change had to be staged with git add --chmod=+x before it would pass.
32 files over cap, down from 33. The three modules are 164, 143 and 105 lines. No Python file in the repo is now over the cap.

risks: A three-way split adds two import edges between sibling modules resolved by bare name on sys.path[0]. That is the existing convention in this directory and the real run confirms it resolves.
The get_media_duration re-export is gone, so any out-of-tree caller importing it from _transcribe_diarize would break. Only transcribe_fw.py imported it, and it was updated in the same commit.
rollback: git revert the commit; _transcribe_diarize.py returns to its 356-line form and the two new modules disappear.
After rollback, confirm python3 transcribe_fw.py /nonexistent.wav still returns 2 and pytest linux_configuration/tests/ reports 338 passed.
